name: LP-MSPM0G5187 LaunchPad development kit
sources: MSPM0G5187 data sheet SLVSJB5B (rev. March 2026, read 2026-10-07: features, NPU, memories, peripherals); LaunchPad user guide SLAU967 (November 2025, read 2026-10-07: kit contents, Table 2-1 jumpers J6 to J25, J101 isolation block, Figure 2-3 BoosterPack pinout, PCM1809 audio ADC and ICS-40720 microphone in the schematic); MSPM0 SDK 2.11.00.07 example READMEs (pins)

columns.head: The chip: MSPM0G5187
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M0+
Runs the program, up to 80 million steps a second (80 MHz). No floating-point unit
Neural accelerator (NPU)
TinyEngine: runs small neural nets in hardware, 2.56 billion operations a second at 80 MHz
Flash: 128 kB / RAM: 32 kB
Same as the LP-MSPM0G3507. Plus 8 kB of data flash
Power: 3.3 V on this board
The chip accepts 1.62 to 3.6 V, so 5 V parts need care

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: USB 2.0 full speed
The chip itself can be a USB device (keyboard, sound card, serial port) or a USB host
I2S audio
The digital audio bus for microphones, DACs and amplifiers. The only MSPM0 family with it
UART, I2C, SPI: 4 shared ports
Each port is set to one job; one SPI runs to 32 Mbit/s
ADC: 1
12-bit voltmeter at 1.6 million samples a second. No 12-bit DAC to make a voltage
AES, CRC
Hardware encryption and checksums. No random-number source or math accelerator listed
Timers: 4
Timing and PWM, up to 14 channels

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
Debug probe with EnergyTrace, microphone into a PCM1809 audio ADC, microSD slot, RGB and red LEDs, 3 buttons
Two USB-C ports
Top: the debug probe. Bottom right: the chip's own USB
Headers
40 pins in four rows (J1 to J4), plus unlabeled extension headers on the underside
Watch out
J6 powers the microphone, audio ADC and SD slot. TI's wake-word example listens on header pin 6, not on the onboard microphone
